unit.why: A brief anecdote quoted from another book praising the Pnei Yehoshua, a non-Hasidic rabbinic authority. It says he studied the whole Talmud 36 times before writing, and that the Maggid of Kozhnitz reported holy spirit in his study hall and a dream he had.
unit.boundary_note: very short; the dream itself is mentioned but not narrated

stories.summary_en: Citing the book Ramatz, the Pnei Yehoshua studied the entire Talmud 36 times before beginning to write, and the Maggid of Kozhnitz said that the holy spirit appeared in his study hall and told of a dream he had.

tags.why: Praise of the Pnei Yehoshua, a non-Hasidic rabbinic authority, quoted from another book

quotes: שקודם שהתחיל לחבר למד ש״ס ל"ו פעמים
tags.why: He studied the whole Talmud 36 times
His study hall is where the holy spirit appeared
A manifestation of the holy spirit in the study hall, though no light or fire is stated

quotes: וסיפר מחלום שהיה לו להפ"י הנ"ל
tags.why: A dream is mentioned but not depicted
